topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the course objectives, scope, and foundational themes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Drivers of cancer, tissue architecture, and cellular modeling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a breakdown in cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations, alongside the methods and limitations of studying these processes in vitro.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, tissue invasion, and stepwise progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the histological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, detailing the mechanisms of invasion, metastatic dissemination, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standardized naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify tumors based on their tissue origin and malignant potential.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical, functional, and systemic processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across human populations and other multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and organ-specific cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the clinical signs of cancer and evaluate the effectiveness and challenges of screening programs across different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Closing housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and practical session arrangements.
